name: What is the difference between a garage conversion and an ADU?

mainEntity.name: How is a garage conversion different from an accessory dwelling unit in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How is a garage conversion different from an accessory dwelling unit in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The difference comes down to function. A garage conversion is the change of use from parking or storage to habitable space. An ADU is a separate residential unit designed for independent living, typically including sleeping, kitchen, and bathroom functions. In Los Angeles-area projects, a garage conversion can be the shell or starting point for an ADU if the homeowner adds the required systems and layout. If the space is used as a bedroom, office, gym, or family room without independent living facilities, it may remain additional living space rather than a separate unit. This distinction affects design, permits, utility planning, and how the property is viewed in the market. It also influences the project budget because a full ADU generally requires more plumbing, mechanical work, and finishes. Homeowners should define the end goal before plans are drawn, since changing from “extra room” to “ADU” midstream often causes rework. The clearest strategy is to match the conversion scope to the intended use from day one.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion is a project that turns an existing garage into habitable space, while an ADU is a self-contained residential unit with its own kitchen and usually its own bathroom. Not every garage conversion becomes an ADU, but many do when the owner wants a separate living unit.
